clue.text: Old poet making for dull study

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: A poet of long ago was produced by tedious academic work.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the seventeenth-century English Poet Laureate, so he fits a poet of the past.

clue.text: Libertine new in French city

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine

explanation.surface: A rake newly arrived in a provincial town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is the Normandy capital on the Seine, a city of France.

clue.text: Stress in journey back to base

definitions.meaning: to emphasise a point forcefully until it registers
literally a car trip back to one's own house

explanation.surface: Travelling home at the end of the day can be stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise an argument is idiomatically to hammer it in; a motorist's return trip is literally that phrase.

clue.text: Count me out concerning concept

parts.note: someone refusing to join says 'not I'
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take part in anything to do with an abstract idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or conception held in the mind, a synonym for concept.

clue.text: Person who supports our present monarch

definitions.meaning: one who backs a motion formally in a meeting
at the time of printing the queen was Elizabeth the Second, styled ER

explanation.surface: A loyal subject backs the reigning queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabetha Regina) was the royal cipher of Elizabeth II, the monarch when this was set; the second sense reads the answer as SECOND ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who backs a proposal in a debate is its seconder; the queen was Elizabeth the Second, ER.

clue.text: Flag single reform with hard speech properly delivered

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner

indicators.note: reform tells us to reshape the letters of the word single

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A campaign for one reform with a banner and a tough message, all spoken correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard English is the accepted form of the language; 'Flag' looks like a verb meaning tire but is the noun for a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The accepted correct form of the language is what careful, properly spoken usage follows.

clue.text: Member of Franciscan order is primate

definitions.meaning: a friar of the hooded reformed branch of the Franciscans
a South American monkey named for its hood-like crown of hair

explanation.surface: A friar from a particular order is also a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The friars wear a distinctive hood, and the New World monkey was named after them for its similar cap of fur.

clue.text: Pronounced skill? Not at all!

indicators.note: pronounced tells us the word is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: know-how means practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Asked whether some ability is marked, someone answers with a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a colloquial way of saying in no way whatsoever, an emphatic negative.

clue.text: Change to amber, right? A couple of seconds after, turn red?

indicators.note: change to tells us to alter the letters of amber into a new order

parts.note: two seconds, each abbreviated S

explanation.surface: Traffic lights going amber and then red within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as traffic lights, but 'turn red?' is a playful definition: embarrassing someone makes them blush.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them blush, so a whimsical way of putting it is causing a face to go crimson.

clue.text: Where people are barely able to exercise their freedom

definitions.text: Where people are barely able to exercise their freedom

parts.words: Where people are barely able to exercise their freedom
parts.note: barely suggests hardly at all, but here it means unclothed: a place where people roam free with no clothes on

explanation.surface: A place where liberty is severely restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist holiday site is where people may go about entirely unclothed.

clue.text: Youthful goddess has to live with male

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A young goddess must share her home with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods on Olympus.

clue.text: Like music reproduced in public document

definitions.meaning: music captured on a disc for playback
stated officially and publicly so that it can be cited

explanation.surface: Music that has been copied appears in an official paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded music is pressed onto a disc; a statement made officially is preserved in the public archive.

clue.text: Dramatist's antihero?

definitions.meaning: someone lacking courage, the opposite of a brave hero

explanation.surface: Asking about the antihero in a playwright's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Dramatist's antihero' as 'the dramatist is an antihero': the possessive is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote Private Lives; a craven person lacking bravery is the reverse of a hero.

clue.text: Woman's love for great man

parts.note: her is the possessive pronoun for a woman
love means zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A woman's affection for a man she admires.
explanation.definitionFit: A man celebrated for great deeds or courage is admired as such.

clue.text: English to recall abuse of voting system

indicators.note: abuse tells us to mistreat the letters of to recall, scrambling them

explanation.surface: An Englishman decides to bring to mind how ballots are rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'of voting system' so that it matches an adjective; 'abuse' looks like part of the surface's ballot-rigging story.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to elections and the choosing of representatives by ballot.

clue.text: Force merger of transport systems

definitions.meaning: to push someone hurriedly into acting
trains joined with highways, the two words combined

explanation.surface: Two transport networks are forced together.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush or coerce someone is to steamroller them; the word joins two kinds of transport route.

clue.text: Pragmatic contribution to venture, a list I compiled

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A practical person adds to a project by drawing up a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sensible, practical outlook based on how things really are.

clue.text: Greek character consumed by smaller monster

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the word that follows

parts.note: minor means smaller or lesser
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is eaten by a lesser beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' tempts a figure from Greek legend, apt for the monster, but it is the letter TAU.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed creature in the Cretan labyrinth is a famous mythical beast.

clue.text: Provide set with live broadcast, primarily entertainment?

definitions.text: Provide set with live broadcast, primarily entertainment?

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered tells us the letters of set and live are spread into a new order
primarily means take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Supplying a television with live transmissions, mostly of shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SET and LIVE into TELEVIS, and 'primarily' adds E from entertainment. The whole clue describes what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a programme on air is to give viewers' sets a transmission, typically of entertainment.

clue.text: Allusion taken oddly selectively, moreover

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of Allusion are picked out, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A reference is made strangely and with discrimination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken oddly selectively' takes the odd letters of ALLUSION, A, L, S, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words add a further point, meaning in addition or besides.

clue.text: Humorous publication about a corporation

indicators.note: about means placed around the following letter

parts.note: Punch was a long-running British satirical magazine

explanation.surface: A comic magazine runs a piece on a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is an old jocular word for a big belly. Punch was a British humour weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation in old slang means a large protruding stomach, the same thing as a pot belly.

clue.text: Boss and I love a creative workplace

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
love means zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: The employer and I adore our artistic office.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or photographer's working room is the place where creative work is made.

clue.text: Remove garment with pockets containing a bunch of keys

indicators.note: pockets as a verb means keeps inside, so the keys hold the next letter

parts.note: four musical keys, D, E, B and G

explanation.surface: Taking off a coat with pockets full of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: The keys are musical: D, E, B, G. DEBAG is British student slang for pulling someone's trousers off as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To debag is to strip a person of their trousers, removing that piece of clothing.

clue.text: Importance of the Romans

parts.note: a Latin word for weight and seriousness, valued by the Romans as a civic virtue

explanation.surface: How significant were the ancient Romans?
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term for dignity and seriousness was one of the prized Roman virtues, now used in English for weightiness.

clue.text: Mostly covering nothing, from the start

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: above means over or covering
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wearing almost no clothes right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of ABOVE to make ABOV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase literally means from the egg, so from the very beginning.

clue.text: Caught wife making baby's bed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so rib is jocular for wife

explanation.surface: A woman is discovered building a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot for an infant is called a crib.

clue.text: A story connected with people's estrangement

parts.note: a story is a lie, an untruth
a nation is a people, read here as 'people is'

explanation.surface: A tale connected with why a people became estranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people's' is read as 'people is', giving NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of isolation or being cut off from others is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Gaol rich, corrupt ruler

indicators.note: corrupt tells us to spoil the order of the letters of gaol rich

explanation.surface: Jail the wealthy, venal head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges GAOLRICH; it looks like an adjective for ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a small group holding power in a state is one of its governing elite.

clue.text: Heroic Trojan bully

definitions.meaning: the greatest warrior of Troy in the Iliad

explanation.surface: A brave warrior of Troy who intimidated others.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam's son was Troy's champion; as a verb the name means to browbeat someone.
